channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Deputy Interior Minister Attends Anti-Terrorism Conference in China
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Interior Minister, Major General Mashrabzoda Jamshed Khol, participated in international events on combating terrorism, extremism, and transnational crime in Lianyungang, China. The conference focused on new security threats, international cooperation, and the use of digital methods to counter extremism.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Trial Defendant Appeals to President for Open Court Proceedings
item.description: Temirlan Sultanbekov, on trial for allegedly attempting to seize power, has written to President Sadyr Japarov requesting an open trial. He has spent over three years in detention and probation, stating he seeks nothing for himself but an open process if authorities are confident in the investigation's fairness.

item.title: Over 96,000 Uzbek Citizens Returned from Russia in 10 Days
item.description: More than 96,000 Uzbek citizens returned to Uzbekistan from Russia in a 10-day period. Over 54,000 came directly from Russia, while the rest transited through Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to citizens facing difficult situations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to fully transition school textbooks to new alphabet by 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to fully transition all school textbooks to the updated Uzbek alphabet between 2027 and 2031. The Deputy Minister of Preschool and School Education, Azizbek Turdiyev, announced this during a Senate session. Textbooks are already updated periodically.

item.title: Five individuals arrested at Namangan airport attempting to smuggle gold to India
item.description: Five people were detained at Namangan International Airport for attempting to illegally export gold worth 1.1 billion soms to India. The suspects, from Andijan and Fergana regions, used their bodies as 'live containers' to hide 555 grams of gold bars and 200 grams of jewelry.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves New 28-Letter Latin-Based Alphabet Variant
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan approved a new variant of the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet, consisting of 28 letters and an apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three digraphs. The proposed reform aims to align writing with the "one sound - one letter" principle and address difficulties encountered since the current alphabet's adoption in 1995. The bill now goes to the president.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces First Robotic Surgery System at Medical Academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's first robot-assisted surgery system was presented at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. The Ministry of Health stated the robot enhances surgeon control, allows minimally invasive procedures, and magnifies the surgical field. It does not replace the surgeon.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election Scheduled for January 27, 2027
item.description: The Zhogorku Kenesh, Kyrgyzstan's parliament, is set to consider scheduling the presidential election for January 27, 2027. The Central Election Commission confirmed the date, noting that the election will proceed even if parliament fails to adopt a resolution. Campaigning is expected to begin in December.

item.title: Uzbekistan to privatize state assets worth over $8 billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has approved a large-scale privatization program. State assets valued at approximately $8 billion, including shares in 84 companies, 1,242 real estate objects, and 8,000 hectares of land, will be put up for open auction. The program also includes the sale of state shares in 18 markets and trade complexes.

item.title: Sogd Region Plans Waste-to-Fertilizer Project with Iranian Partners
item.description: The Sogd Region of Tajikistan and Iranian partners discussed cooperation on upgrading sewage networks and solid waste landfills. They explored implementing modern waste processing technologies to produce organic fertilizers. The project aims to utilize existing expertise from the 'Sabz' company, with initial implementation planned for Khujand and surrounding areas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund Earned 5 Billion Som from State Pension Fund Investments
item.description: From January to August 2026, Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund invested 15.06 billion som from the State Accumulative Pension Fund (SAPF). Investments in government securities yielded 4.35 billion som, while deposits in commercial banks generated 501.8 million som. Dividends from shares added 185.9 million som.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Housing Market Sees 21% Growth in First Seven Months
item.description: Real estate sales in Uzbekistan increased by 21% during January-July, reaching 34,300 transactions. Growth was observed in most regions, with the highest figures recorded in the capital city. This indicates a significant rise in the housing market activity across the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Unveils First Robotic Surgical System at Medical Academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's first robotic surgical system was presented at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. The Ministry of Health stated the system enhances surgical precision and allows for minimally invasive procedures. It does not replace the surgeon's decision-making. Another system is being procured for a maternity hospital.

item.title: Tashkent conducts mass revaluation of real estate; implications for property owners unclear
item.description: Tashkent residents are receiving notifications about the mass revaluation of their property's cadastral value. Many owners are surprised by the significantly different figures presented. Official clarification on the consequences and impact on property taxes is pending, sparking public discussion.

item.title: Two former police officers sentenced to 5 and 6 years for bribery in Sirdaryo
item.description: A court in Sirdaryo region sentenced two former officers from the Khovos district police to 5 and 6 years in prison for demanding bribes. The officers fabricated evidence and demanded money from a farmer, eventually being caught while accepting a portion of the bribe.

item.title: Uzbek citizens returning from abroad can receive grants up to 60 million soms for business expansion
item.description: Uzbek citizens who worked abroad and returned to start businesses can receive grants up to 60 million soms to expand their operations and create jobs. The program, supported by the International Organization for Migration and Sweden, is open to those who returned between 2025-2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares for fish exports to Russia using local feed
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is undergoing certification procedures to ensure uninterrupted fish exports to Russia, using domestically produced feed. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry reported this. The move aims to support local producers and reduce reliance on foreign supplies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament to Consider Presidential Election Date on September 24
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh will review the presidential election appointment on September 24, according to the head of the Central Election Commission. The elections are scheduled for January 27, 2027. Previously, a September 17 date was considered. The election will proceed even if parliament fails to adopt a resolution.

item.title: Sirdaryo Kindergarten Head Fined for Forcing Staff to Collect Votes
item.description: A kindergarten director in Sirdaryo region was fined for compelling staff into forced labor, including cleaning and soliciting votes for an 'Open Budget' initiative. The Ombudsman confirmed violations of the Labor Code. The director faces a fine exceeding 20 million UZS. Such projects will be removed from the budget initiative.

item.title: US Destroys Five Iranian Tankers in Response to Warship Attack
item.description: The US Central Command destroyed five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Hark Island in retaliation for Iran's repeated missile attacks on a US Navy warship. The warship evaded the attacks, and no US personnel were harmed. Iran claimed successful strikes on US destroyers and a Jordanian airbase.

item.title: Solar power plant developer overcharged by nearly 24 million soms
item.description: A company in Kyrgyzstan, granted 800 hectares for a solar power plant, was overcharged compensation payments by over 23.9 million soms, according to the Prosecutor General's Office. The overcharge resulted from an unjustified coefficient applied during calculations for agricultural production losses. Disciplinary action was taken against officials.

item.title: Donald Trump: Vladimir Putin is ready for a deal on Ukraine
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that Russian leader Vladimir Putin is ready to conclude a peace deal with Ukraine. He told Fox News that Putin wants a deal and it would be good if Zelensky also wanted one. Trump mentioned that Putin and Zelensky 'hate each other,' hindering agreement. He also suggested a bilateral meeting with Putin could happen.

item.title: Uzbekistan to consolidate work of local authorities, banks under deputy prime minister
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to hold weekly meetings chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister for work with mahallas to discuss issues related to their activities. A new position, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Association of Uzbek Mahallas, has been established and filled. This official will coordinate the work of local authorities, district organizations, and banks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Significantly Reduces Poverty Rates Ahead of Schedule
item.description: Uzbekistan is reducing poverty faster than projected, with the poverty rate falling from 17% in 2021 to an estimated 4.5% by 2026. This decline is attributed to job creation, entrepreneurship support, and increased use of household plots for income, alongside reduced inequality.

item.title: Bukhara Region and USA Expand Economic and Tourism Ties
item.description: The Bukhara region of Uzbekistan and the United States are strengthening economic and tourism cooperation. Discussions between the regional governor and the US deputy ambassador focused on investment potential, economic opportunities, tourism resources, and ongoing joint projects in agriculture and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews Employment and Income Growth Initiatives
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev critically reviewed regional efforts to boost employment and increase public income. A new system assigns regional and district-level responsibilities to khokims, with employment agencies and economic structures tasked with local job creation and income enhancement. Some officials were noted for failing to engage directly with communities and businesses.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Regulate Illegally Occupied Land Around Apartment Buildings
item.description: Uzbekistan may offer land plots for private kindergartens, schools, and technical schools at a starting price of 1 million soums for auction if entrepreneurs commit to educating children from needy families for free. This initiative aims to provide employment for parents and quality education for children.

item.title: Building Valued at $1.2 Million Returned to State Ownership in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A building and a 23,500 square meter land plot in Naryn, Kyrgyzstan, valued at approximately 96.5 million soms (about $1.2 million), have been returned to state ownership. The property was illegally transferred to private hands in 2003 by officials violating land legislation.

item.title: Canada Imposes 50% Tariffs on US Goods in Response to US Trade Measures
item.description: Canada has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on US products starting September 8, retaliating against US President Donald Trump's administration's decision to levy 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The measures cover approximately CAD 27.6 billion in imports and include steel, aluminum, dairy, and electronics.

item.title: Uzbekistan's growing international interest highlighted by foreign media
item.description: Foreign media partners have focused on Uzbekistan's developments, including economic activity, tourism, and digital transformation. Publications from Anadolu and TASS noted the establishment of a strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia, with leaders signing a joint declaration and agreements on cooperation in agriculture, tourism, and culture.

item.title: SCO cooperation in AI can shape a shared digital future, referencing Al-Khwarizmi
item.description: The Bishkek Declaration calls for safe and responsible AI use, ensuring it does not harm human life or undermine state sovereignty. Uzbekistan's IT Park representative highlighted the region's historical connection to AI through mathematician Al-Khwarizmi, whose work on algorithms is foundational to modern AI development.

item.title: Uzbekistan may allow first-floor apartments for business without reclassification
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes allowing the use of first-floor apartments in multi-story buildings for commercial purposes without reclassifying them as non-residential. This aims to facilitate small businesses like shops and service centers, simplifying the current complex process of obtaining permits.

item.title: SCO summit in Bishkek expands agenda beyond security to economic cooperation
item.description: The 25th anniversary Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek marked a significant milestone, expanding its focus beyond traditional security issues. Discussions included trade, economic cooperation, investment, transport, energy, digitalization, and artificial intelligence, reflecting a comprehensive approach to Eurasian development. The summit reaffirmed the 'Shanghai Spirit' of mutual trust and consensus.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares application for Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing its country application for support from the Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI) for the 2026-2030 period. A GAVI mission visited Bishkek for a working group meeting on the application, attended by health officials and representatives from WHO and UNICEF.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares application for Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing a country application for support from the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI) for the 2026-2030 period. A working group meeting, attended by health officials and international partners, discussed the application for GAVI 6.0 funding.

item.title: Spanish investors explore opening four and five-star hotels in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Tourism Committee met with Barceló Hotel Group to discuss tourism development. The Spanish company is interested in building four and five-star hotels and managing existing tourist facilities. This interest highlights Uzbekistan's growing attractiveness to foreign investors and its tourism potential.

item.title: German company sees rapid development in Uzbekistan's textile industry
item.description: Thomas Gnoht of Optibelt GmbH expressed interest in Uzbekistan's dynamic economic reforms, particularly in the textile sector. The company, a supplier of drive belts, sees Uzbekistan as a promising market and plans to expand cooperation and sales. They are pleased with the rapid growth of the textile industry.

item.title: Brent crude oil price surpasses $100 per barrel for first time since July
item.description: Brent crude oil futures on the ICE exchange in London traded above $100 per barrel on September 9. The price increase of over 2 percent for November delivery is attributed to renewed tensions between the US and Iran, raising concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

item.title: Kyrgyz activist claims authorities attempted to arrest him in Cambodia
item.description: Political blogger and activist Syrgak Kenzhebaev stated that Kyrgyz authorities attempted to arrest him in Cambodia on August 31. Previously, he released a video alleging that the president's brother and relatives are involved in political matters and customs in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia preparing zero-tariff free trade agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have begun work on a free trade agreement that will establish zero tariff rates for goods on a mutual basis. The agreement is expected to create favorable conditions for Uzbek products in the Serbian market. Both countries have also adopted a separate program for industrial cooperation.
